name: Southeast Ridge (SE Corner)

pitch_detail.notes: Scrambling from the Pyramid notch on solid rock with ample protection.
Low 5th class moves on quality rock to the summit; about 5.3 with selective route-finding; holding strictly to the crest adds two steps near 5.6 and 5.7.

rappel_detail.notes: First of the gully rappels. A 60 m rope reaches between all the standard stations.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed rap ring on webbing, or a slung horn
hazards: The gully is a rockfall corridor, worse late in the season and when several parties are stacked in it.
rappel_detail.station: The head of the central gully, just below the summit block after the short downclimb from the top.

rappel_detail.notes: Second gully rappel. With a 30 m rope, expect short downclimbs to link stations.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed webbing or a slung horn
hazards: Inspect the webbing before use; worn rings and slings are replaced only periodically.
rappel_detail.station: A station midway down the central gully.

rappel_detail.notes: Last gully rappel, onto the snow at the top of the Sulphide Glacier. Late in the season, with more rock exposed, some parties add a fourth short rappel here.
rappel_detail.anchor: fixed station or a slung horn
rappel_detail.station: The lower gully, near the base of the summit pyramid.

rappels: Usually 3 rappels down the summit pyramid's central gully (two to four by snow cover); a 60 m rope reaches all stations
descent_text: Rappel the same 4th-class gully used as the standard ascent line up the summit pyramid (the line shared with the Fisher Chimneys/Sulphide Glacier finish); a 60m rope reaches all belay stations.
approach: East-northeast up Shannon Ridge, then traverse Sulphide Glacier to reach southeast ridge base
overview: The classic technical finish to Shuksan's Summit Pyramid, climbed after approaching via Fisher Chimneys or Sulphide Glacier: six pitches of good-quality rock up to 5.3 gaining the pyramid's SE corner.
beta: Grade 5.3-5.7, II-III Alpine. 600 vertical feet over 6 pitches from ridge base to summit. Rock quality excellent. Primary hazards: high exposure, significant glacier crevasses, late-season ice conditions, Class 4 downclimbing. 60m rope required for descent rappels. Accessible via Sulphide Glacier or Fisher Chimneys approaches. Often requires bivy camp due to multi-day approach.
face: SE side of the Summit Pyramid
